overview: After 1.h4 c5 2.b4, White offers the b-pawn to open the long diagonal for a bishop on b2 and the b-file. Black can take on b4, play ...Qa5 or ...d5, and usually ends a pawn up with a sound position. Both kings are safe for now, so the gambit lives on White's queenside pressure.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Bb2 and Nf3, hitting the long diagonal and b-file
Use h4 only as a waiting or flank-expansion move

black_ideas.idea: Take on b4 and develop with ...Nf6, ...d5 and ...Nc6
Keep the centre and the extra pawn

typical_structures.structure: Open queenside after cxb4; Black centre pawns vs White flank pawns

character.notes: An irregular flank gambit that is more strange than tactical; the extra pawn is easy to hold.

gambit.notes: White offers b4, and ...cxb4 wins a pawn that can be kept.

soundness.notes: Strong players do not rate 1.h4 and 2.b4 as sufficient compensation.

structure.notes: Centre undecided, with pawns coming off on the queenside.

approach.notes: Almost never played by strong players, chosen for surprise.

sublines_that_differ.name: 1.h4 e5 2.d4 exd4 3.c3
sublines_that_differ.how: A different reply with a central gambit; most database games begin this way.

character.reason: Gambit with offbeat open lines, but little concrete tactics.

gambit.reason: White offers the b-pawn and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: An unproven pawn offer with h4 played for no developmental reason.

structure.reason: The centre is not yet decided.

plans.reason: White's b4 push and Bb2 is a queenside space grab.
